subsystems.name: Helicon plasma source
subsystems.role: turns neutral gas into a dense, cold plasma without electrodes.

subsystems.name: Ion-cyclotron heating stage
subsystems.role: adds energy to the plasma with radio waves tuned to the ion motion, raising its temperature enormously.

subsystems.name: Magnetic nozzle
subsystems.role: a shaped magnetic field that opens out and converts the plasma's random thermal energy into a directed exhaust — no physical nozzle to erode.

subsystems.name: Superconducting magnet stack
subsystems.role: generates the steady kilotesla-scale field that contains and guides the plasma.

subsystems.name: Radio-frequency power and control
subsystems.role: supplies tens of kilowatts to megawatts of radio-frequency power and splits it between the two stages.

subsystems.name: Spacecraft power and thermal system
subsystems.role: supplies the large electrical input and rejects the waste heat.

buildSteps.title: Fix the magnetic field shape
buildSteps.detail: Coil positions and currents are designed so the field is strongest in the source, rises through the heating section and then diverges steadily to form the nozzle.

buildSteps.title: Wind and test the magnets
buildSteps.detail: Solenoids are wound from superconducting cable and cooled to a few tens of kelvin by cryocoolers, then tested for field strength and quench behaviour.

buildSteps.title: Build the source and antennas
buildSteps.detail: A ceramic tube carries the helical first-stage antenna; a second antenna sits in the stronger field downstream. Both are vacuum-compatible and matched to their amplifiers.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the core on one axis
buildSteps.detail: Source, heating section and nozzle are stacked and aligned so the plasma stays centred and never touches a wall.

buildSteps.title: Add radio-frequency power and control
buildSteps.detail: Power amplifiers feed the two antennas; control software shifts power between stages to trade thrust against exhaust velocity at constant electrical input.

buildSteps.title: Wire in power and radiators
buildSteps.detail: Hundreds of kilowatts to megawatts of electrical power arrive from arrays or a reactor, and a coolant loop carries waste heat to radiators sized for the duty cycle.

buildSteps.title: Ground-test in a vacuum chamber
buildSteps.detail: The engine is fired for hundreds of hours at rising power while a thrust stand measures force in newtons and probes map the exhaust plume and magnetic field.

buildSteps.title: Qualify for flight
buildSteps.detail: A flight-representative unit goes through vibration, thermal-vacuum and long-duration life testing, including repeated thermal cycling of the cryogenic magnets.

buildSteps.title: Fly a demonstrator
buildSteps.detail: A spacecraft flies the engine for months, measuring thrust, hours of operation, plume interaction with solar arrays and any long-term drift in performance.

prerequisites.why: a useful high-thrust version needs far more power than any spacecraft has generated; the largest orbital arrays are around a hundred kilowatts and space fission reactors have flown only at kilowatt scale.
cryocoolers fly routinely on telescopes, but a large superconducting solenoid has not operated on a spacecraft for years at a time.
the tens-of-megahertz drive electronics exist on the ground but need space qualification at the hundreds-of-kilowatts level.

prerequisites.tech: Electric propulsion flight heritage and thrust measurement
prerequisites.why: gridded ion and Hall thrusters already fly commercially, giving mission planners experience with low-thrust trajectories and power budgets.
steady high-power operation produces waste heat that must be radiated away, constraining the whole spacecraft design.

pathway.milestone: ground testing of a ~200 kW prototype, producing a few newtons of thrust in a vacuum chamber
pathway.unlocks: demonstration that the electrodeless two-stage concept works at power levels useful for space.

pathway.milestone: an in-orbit demonstrator running for hundreds of hours
pathway.unlocks: lifetime data on magnets, antennas and thermal control in the real space environment; a proposed test on the International Space Station was not carried out.

pathway.milestone: 100 kW-class solar-electric space tugs for orbit raising and cargo transport
pathway.unlocks: cheaper movement of payloads to high orbits and to the Moon, where chemical stages are very mass-hungry.

pathway.milestone: megawatt nuclear-electric engines for crewed interplanetary trips
pathway.unlocks: transit times of a few months to Mars, because high exhaust velocity plus high power means much less propellant.
